clue.text: All in, cold buffet

parts.note: something dead is cold and lifeless
to buffet is to strike or beat

explanation.surface: Someone worn out, offered nothing but a cold spread of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal but is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All in' is informal for utterly exhausted, which is what dead beat means.

clue.text: Replacin' the soundtrack for Grease

definitions.meaning: dubbing a film means replacing its soundtrack; the clipped spelling matches the dropped G
a greasy preparation for softening and waterproofing leather

explanation.surface: A note that the musical Grease had its songs re-recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Replacin'' signals the clipped form, dubbin' for dubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a waxy leather dressing, a kind of grease rubbed into boots.

clue.text: Guarantee cry of pain after case of Viagra's used up

indicators.note: the cry of pain is placed after the reversed pair
in a down clue, 'up' sends the picked letters upwards, so they read backwards
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: ouch is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A grumble that a pill's packaging hurt to open, or a joke about its side effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes V and A from Viagra; 'used up' turns them to AV.
explanation.definitionFit: To avouch is an old word for to affirm or vouch for, so to guarantee.

clue.text: Spreads content leaving bloggers' cycling thread on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship is sitting between its outer letters, as in the familiar S...S wrap
with the contents gone, only the outside letters of the word remain
cycling moves letters round from the front of the word to its end

explanation.surface: A web forum thread keeps going round in circles among bloggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the first two letters of thread to its end; 'content leaving' strips bloggers to its shell, and 'on board' places one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadths are widths or extents, how far something spreads.

clue.text: Doctor depicts pain involving bit of intestine with this complaint

indicators.note: the anagram takes in the extra letter among its own
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged
a small bit of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A physician sketches the pain of a patient whose gut is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges DEPICTS PAIN into APPENDICTIS, and 'involving' adds I from intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendicitis is an illness, inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch of the bowel.

clue.text: French cultural organisation withdraw Monet's one artwork

indicators.note: to withdraw something is to pull it out of the word

parts.note: UNESCO is the UN's educational, scientific and cultural organisation
Monet was French, and the French for one is un

explanation.surface: A French cultural body pulls a Monet painting from display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monet's one' is not a painting but the French word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Vicar meets a politician and pimp

parts.note: a vicar is addressed as Rev, Reverend
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: a clergyman, an MP and a pimp all meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pimp' is the slang verb to do up, as in 'pimp my ride'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pimp something in slang is to smarten it up, which is to revamp it.

clue.text: French race track's finale elevated by South African representative, perhaps

indicators.note: the closing letter is lifted higher up the word, as this is a down clue

parts.note: Le Mans is the French circuit of the 24-hour motor race

explanation.surface: A finish at a French motor race is moved up the order by a South African driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The S ending Le Mans moves up to give LESMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative is a commercial traveller selling a firm's goods, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Hide under excessive clothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the hide word sits beneath the other

parts.note: over means too much, as in overdone
an animal's hide is its coat

explanation.surface: Someone hides from view by wearing far too many clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat is a heavy outer garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Olympian takes a little paracetamol after surprise parties

indicators.note: the god comes after the startling cry

parts.note: boo is a cry used to give someone a fright or surprise

indicators.note: the god's name takes in the extra letter

parts.note: Zeus is the chief of the gods on Mount Olympus

indicators.note: a little of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An athlete reaches for painkillers after a shock party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' means a god of Olympus, not an athlete. P goes inside ZEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze-ups are informal British words for heavy drinking parties.

clue.text: Restyle Elvis occasionally, coming back lithe …

indicators.note: coming back means the picked letters are read from right to left
only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A makeover for the slimmed-down Elvis, returning to his trim youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'Restyle Elvis', E T L E V S, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful, close to lithe and supple.

clue.text: Cigarette butt from corpse keeps me over a barrel, identifying a variety of contacts

indicators.note: the cigarette-plus-letter keeps the rest inside it

parts.note: gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette

indicators.note: a butt is the end of something, so the last letter is taken
in a down clue this goes above what follows it

parts.note: taken as written
BL is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a cigarette end found at a corpse puts the narrator at someone's mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cigarette butt' looks like one item, but the cigarette and the butt work separately; 'over a barrel' is not the idiom here.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas-permeable lenses are rigid contact lenses that let oxygen through to the eye.

clue.text: … and slim in cute pants, in charge for film soundtrack, maybe

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are poor and rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 10: Elvis, slim in cute trousers, is put in charge of a film score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is the slang adjective for bad, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music is background music accompanying a film or play, its score.

clue.text: Weaklings save seconds — swapping cold for hot

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another, as the clue spells out

parts.note: to scrimp is to save by being frugal
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Feeble people save a few seconds by turning the shower from cold to hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimps is a slang term for small or feeble people, puny types.

clue.text: Average American soldier

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

explanation.surface: A description of a typical GI, an average American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American soldier' looks like one phrase, but only 'soldier' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A para is a paratrooper, a soldier trained to parachute into action.

clue.text: Write about love — a newspaper man's first — expressed in legal document

indicators.note: the newspaper worker's title comes first in the answer

parts.note: a sub, or subeditor, works on a newspaper

indicators.note: the writing word goes about, around, the other

parts.note: to pen is to write
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A journalist writes about love, with the paper's editor first, in a court filing.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside PEN to give POEN, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ ordering someone to attend court, a legal document.

clue.text: Quote bareheaded, ancient, Celtic priest, looking towards the stars — it'll get you going

indicators.note: facing upwards; in a down clue the letters then read from the bottom up

parts.note: to cite is to quote

indicators.note: with its head removed, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a druid was a priest of the ancient Celts

explanation.surface: A druid stargazing at the solstice, quoted as saying he is ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: CITE plus RUID, read upwards as the clue is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A diuretic is a drug increasing urine flow: humorously, it sends you to the toilet.

clue.text: Call one out following poor BAME representation — prepare defence

indicators.note: the call comes after the rearranged letters
a poor version of the word is a jumbled one

parts.note: the letters standing for Black, Asian and minority ethnic, a British umbrella label

indicators.note: one is put out of the word

parts.note: to title something is to call it by a name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone calls out the poor representation of Black, Asian and minority ethnic people, then braces for backlash.
explanation.walkthrough: BAME (Black, Asian and minority ethnic) is a British label. Its jumble is EMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to arrange forces for battle or fortify, readying a defence.

clue.text: Universal veto for operating system

parts.note: U is the film classification abbreviation for universal
to nix is to forbid or veto

explanation.surface: A worldwide ban on some computer software.
explanation.definitionFit: Unix is a multi-user computer operating system developed at Bell Labs.

clue.text: Display some ingredients of garibaldi — or a macaroon

indicators.note: a few of the letters that make up these words, in a row

explanation.surface: A biscuit display shows what goes into a garibaldi or a macaroon.
explanation.walkthrough: A garibaldi is a British biscuit with a currant layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model scene, a display such as in a museum.

clue.text: Earl and headless monster going out

indicators.note: without its head, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre, a monster

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a beheaded monster leave the scene together.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of leaving a place; the noun matches 'going out' as a noun.

clue.text: Tolkien's goblins recalled essence of yellow parchment, say

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: orcs are the goblin soldiers in Tolkien's Lord of the Rings

indicators.note: the essence of something is its heart, the middle letters

explanation.surface: Tolkien's orcs remembered a scrap of old yellowed parchment.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of YELLOW is LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scroll is a rolled sheet of writing material, such as a parchment roll.

clue.text: Desperate U-turn over Europe, ultimately deceptive

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumble sits over the final letter
a desperate version of the word is wildly disordered
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: A political headline about a desperate policy reversal on Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' rearranges UTURN into UNTRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is false, so it misleads like a deceptive claim.

clue.text: Evita's touring cast feel caring, delivering flyer

indicators.note: the surname goes around the rest, like a tour

parts.note: Evita was Eva Perón of Argentina

indicators.note: cast is used of moulding or throwing, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: The touring cast of Evita feel warm and caring as they deliver the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors but rearranges FEEL CARING into EGRINEFALC.
explanation.definitionFit: A peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey, a winged hunter.

clue.text: Judge in drug haze reportedly

indicators.note: as reported in speech, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug, and steam is a haze

explanation.surface: A judge caught in a drug-induced haze, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus STEAM, said aloud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem in an older sense is to consider or reckon, to judge.

clue.text: A battalion rebel over scene of bloodshed

parts.note: Bat. is an abbreviation for battalion

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to riot is to rebel

explanation.surface: A battalion mutinies, and bloodshed follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse, literally a place where blood is shed.

clue.text: Confront accountant about expenditure

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
cost is the outlay or expenditure

explanation.surface: Taking on an accountant over the matter of spending.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost is to approach and address someone boldly, to confront them.

clue.text: Well I never! Disheartened after wife leaves, returning to cause some kind of alarm

indicators.note: coming back, so the letters read in the reverse direction
with its heart taken away, the middle letter goes
when the wife leaves, her letter is taken out of the phrase

explanation.surface: An exclamation from someone heartbroken after their wife walks out, then comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W leaves ELLINEVER; its heart N goes, leaving ELLIEVER, which reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the military bugle call to wake soldiers, a morning alarm.
